name: Queenstown
summary: Queenstown on Lake Wakatipu: every roof measured by LINZ's 2021 LiDAR under its 2026 aerial photos, the Skyline Gondola to Bob's Peak, the TSS Earnslaw at Steamer Wharf, and the Remarkables across the lake.

guide.line: The adventure capital of the south, folded between Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Ride the gondola up at dusk, watch the lake turn to gold, and be on the wharf when the old steamer whistles.
spots: Up to Bob's Peak, the whole lake beneath you
A 1912 coal-fired steamer, still sailing every day
A jagged wall of rock across the water, snow-capped till spring
local: Local
Kāi Tahu named the bay Tāhuna. Today it's a burger after midnight and a Central Otago pinot on the waterfront.

name: Sydney
summary: Central Sydney: 7,962 buildings, the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, sun access on protected public places, and a game: walk it, ride the ferries, fly under the bridge.

guide.line: A harbour city of sails and sandstone. Take the ferry past the Opera House, wander The Rocks where the colony began, and watch the bridge light up as the sun goes down behind Balmain.
spots: Utzon's white sails on Bennelong Point
The Coathanger: fly beneath its steel arch
Green-and-gold ferries out to Manly and Taronga
local: Local
Gadigal Country for tens of thousands of years. Today: a flat white at dawn, a ferry to work, fish and chips on the quay.

guide.hook: Kyoto Tower's beacon, Nishiki Market and the Imperial Palace gardens

guide.line: The glass valley of Kyoto Station, its 171 steps to the sky garden, and Kyoto Tower's candle across the road.

Kyoto's kitchen: pickles, tofu and grilled skewers down a narrow covered market, a few streets from the Kamo River.
The shoguns' castle in the emperor's city: painted gold rooms and floors that sing like nightingales.
A thousand years of emperors behind long earthen walls, and Gyoen's gravel avenues under plum and cherry.
The vermilion Romon at the end of Shijo-dori, the lanterns of the dance hall, and Gion's lanes beyond.
Five storeys over the tiled roofs: the pagoda every photograph of old Kyoto is framed around.
Stone steps between wooden teahouses and pottery shops, lantern-lit at dusk, all the way up to Kiyomizu.
The wooden stage on its lattice of keyaki pillars, thirteen metres over the trees, and the Otowa spring below.
The Romon guarded by stone foxes, and the two tunnels of the Senbon Torii climbing into the woods.
Halfway up Mount Inari through thousands of torii, the whole city spread out below at the crossroads.
The Silver Pavilion that was never silvered, its sand cone and its moss garden under the eastern hills.
Two kilometres of stone path along a canal under cherry trees, the walk a philosopher took every morning.
The great Sanmon gate, a red-brick aqueduct running through a Zen temple, and the old Keage Incline.
Japan's capital for a thousand years, and it still keeps the old hours: temple bells at dawn, lanterns in the lanes at dusk, and some 1,600 temples tucked between the hills.

name: Marunouchi & Ginza

tagline: Tokyo Station, the Palace, Ginza, the water bus and Tokyo Tower

group_meta.summary: Tokyo as maps, the way games draw it: each district a walkable map of its own, chosen from the subway map. Lit stations are built; grey ones are next.
group_meta.note: Districts and lines from the Tokyo Metro and JR East maps; station positions are the stations' own (OpenStreetMap). Which districts a game sends you to follows Persona 5's Tokyo (Atlus, 2016): Shibuya, Shinjuku, Akihabara, Asakusa, Ueno, Ikebukuro, Odaiba, Jinbocho, Kanda, Tsukishima.

guide.line: Red-brick Tokyo Station, glass towers and the moats and stone walls of the Imperial Palace.
Tokyo's grand boulevard: flagship stores, Wako's clock tower and the water bus down to Tokyo Tower.
The world's busiest crossing, the faithful dog Hachiko, and the whole city at your feet from SHIBUYA SKY.
Crepes and street fashion on Takeshita Street, and the hush of Meiji Jingu's forest next door.
Neon Kabukicho, Golden Gai's six-seat bars, and the towers of Nishi-Shinjuku lit up at night.
Quiet backstreets, a ginkgo avenue turning gold, and the Suga Shrine stairs from Your Name.
Old izakaya alleys in the Sankaku Chitai, a corner bathhouse, and the Tokyo the tour buses miss.
Electric Town: arcades stacked six floors high, anime shops and maid cafés under the neon.
Old Edo: the Thunder Gate's great red lantern, incense smoke at Senso-ji, and rice crackers fresh off the grill.
Tokyo Skytree, 634 m, the tallest tower in the world, rising over the Sumida River.
Museums under the cherry trees, the lotus pond, and Ameyoko's market stalls beneath the tracks.
Sunshine City, Otome Road's anime shops and a bowl of ramen long after the last train.

Art by day and clubs till dawn: the view from Mori Tower and the giant spider Maman.
Monja Street: griddles sizzling in a riverside island town of old wooden houses.
Rainbow Bridge across the bay, a life-size Gundam, and a beach with the skyline beyond.
The Tokaido's first stop: bullet trains, and Sengaku-ji where the forty-seven ronin rest.
Thirty-seven million people, and every station opens onto a different world. Pick a stop on the line and step out into it.
